question: What was the speed of the car if it travelled 150 km of distance in 3 hrs?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct Application of Speed Formula:

**Speed** = **Distance** ÷ **Time**

**Speed** = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total Distance** = 150 km

**Total Time** = 3 hrs

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33bde733a46e99df5551af58ee7c6ffa61671ead2f29838663296214f1d0acff.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed = 150 km / 3 hrs

⇒ Speed = 50 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

**Average Speed** = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time). If distances are equal, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y) where x and y are individual speeds.

Relative Speed

For objects moving in the **same direction**, subtract speeds (S₁ − S₂). For **opposite directions**, add speeds (S₁ + S₂).</p
